units.unit: Hong Kong should tighten rent control on subdivided units because tenants are exploited
Needs evidence about rents and tenant conditions
Needs a counter-view about landlords
D1 is a primer to learn who lives in SDUs and what the debate is
D2 has rent data over time needed as evidence of rents
SDU tenants pay a per-square-foot premium
Rent burden rose from 31 to 34 percent
Wants a counter-view from landlords and from supply theory
Landlords say a hard cap would make owners exit
D2p1 shows stock kept growing after the 2021 ordinance
Moderate tightening, like capping initial rents modestly, did not cause exit
Argues for tightening in a moderate form
D5 gives the landlord side that must be answered
D6 is academic work on rent control types and supply, to separate moderate from hard caps
D2p1 shows stable stock under an increase cap only (D6p2)
Now argues Hong Kong should tighten second-generation controls, like limiting increases and giving tenure security, not hard initial-rent caps
D6p1 says hard caps remove 3 to 5 percent of stock
D5p3 shows landlords have weak data
A hard cap would be enforced thinly because tenants with no written agreement and newest arrivals cannot complain, so the worst-off get protected last
Tenants say the real problem is insecurity and the long public-housing queue, not rent
Tenants would trade rent for security of tenure
D10 is about enforcement missing the most exploited tenants
D4 is a tenant with no written agreement
D11 is the tenant survey on tenure security versus rent
Needs the interview with the tenant who talks about notice periods and the queue
The interview would support the claim that tenants name insecurity and the queue as the worst part, with a tenant's own account of a short notice period
Mr Chan's own account of the notice period and the queue backs the claim that tenants name insecurity as the worst part
Mrs Wong supports a hard cap and says landlords would not leave
Her own interview notes two flats converted to storage, so her view does not show landlords stay
D6p2 says second-generation controls have small effects on stock, which is why stable stock after 2021 fits an increase cap and not a hard cap
Enforcement is the other problem: only 6 percent of stock is inspected
